label: miso 57 rdt congestion
definition: miso-57 RDT congestion depth: the miso-56 keeper recipe replayed from its exhaustive meta.json (strict replay -- errors on unmapped keys) with exactly two structural changes, zero fitted scalars. (1) miso_south_seam_split: the South seam's reference-price bands re-home onto their own external zone (split_miso_south_external_node), severing the shared MISO_external bus's free South->external->Midwest wheel around the RDT contract path -- a fabricated cost-free 3,000 MW bypass a 2025 diagnostic probe measured at 1,255 MW summer mean (7.7 TWh/yr) while the RDT S->N link carried 54 MW mean and saturated 13 h/yr, against the IMM's measured $9.31/MWh summer-2025 Midwest-South separation. (2) miso_rdt_tcdc: the static JOA contract limits (3,000 N->S / 2,500 S->N) become the published operating representation -- the 92% default derate (2024 SOM III.B) as the free tier, then the two-step RDT Transmission Constraint Demand Curve ($40/MWh at the modeled limit, $500/MWh from 102%, hard bound at contract) as priced one-way tiers (TransferLink.flow_cost; MISO/SPP JOA Attach. A). Result: RDT reproduces measured behaviour in-window -- 2023/24 S->N 1,139/1,035 MW (measured 917/1,108), binds 27%/25% of hours (measured >25% 2024), separation-when-binding $2.77/$2.89 (measured ~$3). Score NOT-YET (FAIL fuelmix/sysvol/price_mean/price_tail/co2, carried from miso-56): 2025 annual C3a -13.3% -> -11.7%, July-2025 -18.8 unchanged (ELMP/emergency drivers, other lanes), August 2023/24 clean +0.5/+0.5, D-2 CT 5.8/3.7/8.1% vs 15% cap. The 2025 gap is root-caused to an UPSTREAM RDT direction reversal (model runs N->S 29% / S->N 4%; reality ran S->N) driven by the standing COAL_BIT/CC mid-merit split -- the constraint that will price the separation is now in place and validated on 2023-24 (FINDING sec 11).
market_story: Zero-forcing twin is near-identical (annual load-weighted price within $0.09/MWh all three years; FAIL set one fewer -- drops co2): the fit is carried economically, not by forcing. Both new mechanisms are market structure, not floors -- the South-seam split removes a fabricated free transfer path and the RDT TCDC adds MISO's own published contract-path market design (92% derate + $40/$500 demand curve, all values cited to the 2024 SOM III.B and the MISO/SPP JOA); D-2 attributes 3.7-8.1% of CT energy to the unchanged evening reliability floor (cap 15%), so no forcing was added by this lane. DOF ledger 13 entries, residual count unchanged at 2 (the two offer-curve legacies); both RDT mechanisms enter as measured-physical zero-scalar rows.
